items.followUp: What is a group in the periodic table? Give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies a group as a vertical column and states the shared properties of its elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that elements in the same group form a family and have similar chemical properties.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows how elements in a group are referred to as a family.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct group/family example.

modelAnswer: Elements in the same vertical group of the periodic table are called a family because they have similar chemical properties.
For example, lithium, sodium and potassium belong to Group 1 and are called the alkali-metal family.

items.followUp: Who arranged the elements according to increasing atomic number in the modern periodic table?

rubric.why: Identifies the chemist credited with introducing the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for naming Dmitri Mendeleev.

modelAnswer: Dmitri Mendeleev introduced the periodic table in 1869.

items.followUp: What determines whether an element belongs to the s-block or p-block?

rubric.why: The block classification depends on the subshell receiving the last (differentiating) electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an element's block is determined by the subshell into which its last electron enters.

rubric.why: The four block names complete the definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the s, p, d and f blocks.

modelAnswer: A block is a set of elements in which the last electron enters the same type of subshell.
The periodic table has s, p, d and f blocks.

items.followUp: Define a single covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond involves the sharing of two pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.

rubric.why: A valid molecule containing a double covalent bond is required as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as O₂ or a C=O bond.

modelAnswer: A double covalent bond is formed when two atoms share two pairs of electrons.
For example, the oxygen molecule has a double bond: O=O.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a dilute and a concentrated solution?

rubric.why: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at that temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a saturated solution as holding the maximum soluble amount of solute at a given temperature.

rubric.why: An unsaturated solution can still dissolve additional solute under the stated conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an unsaturated solution can dissolve more solute at that temperature.

modelAnswer: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a given temperature; it cannot dissolve more solute.
An unsaturated solution contains less than this maximum amount and can dissolve more solute at that temperature.

items.followUp: Define reduction in terms of hydrogen and oxygen.

rubric.why: Oxidation includes the gain or addition of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining oxidation as gain or addition of oxygen.

rubric.why: Oxidation also includes the removal or loss of hydrogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining oxidation as removal or loss of hydrogen.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the gain or addition of oxygen.
Oxidation is also the removal or loss of hydrogen.

items.followUp: Write two physical characteristics of non-metals.

rubric.why: Any one correct physical characteristic of metals earns this mark.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct characteristic, such as lustre, malleability, ductility, conductivity or sonority.

rubric.why: A second distinct correct characteristic is required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct physical characteristic of metals.

modelAnswer: Metals are malleable and can be hammered into sheets.

items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of magnesium much higher than its second ionization energy?

rubric.why: After the first ionization, the second electron is removed from the 3s subshell of Mg⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that the second electron is removed from Mg⁺, which has configuration [Ne]3s¹.

rubric.why: The electron is more strongly attracted in the positively charged ion, so more energy is needed than for the first ionization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the positively charged ion attracts the remaining electron more strongly, requiring more energy.

modelAnswer: Magnesium has the electron configuration [Ne]3s²; after the first ionization, Mg⁺ has the configuration [Ne]3s¹.
The second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion, where it experiences greater attraction, so more energy is required than for the first ionization.
